0.long_answer: Colchicine is a drug commonly used to treat calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate crystal deposition disease. It is effective in reducing inflammation and pain caused by the deposition of calcium pyrophosphate crystals in the joints. Colchicine is known to interact with both the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transporter and the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP3A4. These interactions are particularly important because drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 or P-gp can increase the toxicity of colchicine, especially in patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency.
